Letter from Steve Kubby Calling For Senator Vasconcellos to Open
Medical Marijuana Summit To Other Views.

May 23, 1998
K U B B Y  F O R  G O V E R N O R 1998 CALIFORNIA 2002
STATEWIDE CAMPAIGN OFFICE
Voice: (714) 537-9200
Fax: (714) 537-9203
Toll Free: (877) GO-KUBBY
http://www.kubby.com

To Richard Cowan
Editor, Marijuana News

Dear Dick,

I’m grateful for your support and for publishing a copy of our Community Based Model for Medical Marijuana See

Letter to Senator Vasconcellos On Medical Marijuana Summit From Colorado Citizens for Compassionate Cannabis

To Richard Cowan
Editor, Marijuana News

Dear Dick,

I’m grateful for your support and for publishing a copy of our Community Based Model for Medical Marijuana See

Ben Franklin warned that those who trade security for liberty will soon have neither. Yet that’s the road that Americans for Medical Rights (AMR) and Vasconcellos are taking everyone. We don’t need more legislation to police patients, but we could sure use some legislation to police the government officials who are violating the rights of patients.

Vasco still has time to make this a real Summit, by including those who put Prop. 215 on the ballot in these important discussions. Unfortunately, the evidence suggests a deliberate attempt to silence any opposition to a law enforcement model of medical marijuana distribution.

Just look at how real debate is being stifled and patients are being harmed:

Please join me, Laura Kriho, Jeff Jones, Kirk Warren (Prop. 215 treasurer), and Robert Raich (the Oakland CBC’s attorney) in demanding that the Community Based Model for Medical Marijuana Distribution be officially recognized by this Summit and that time be allotted to present our arguments for why patients don’t want photo IDs or police involvement in their health care decisions.

Let freedom ring,

Steve

(Ed. note: I agree with everything that Steve Kubby says here. I also think that there are better ways of distributing medical marijuana.
See

It is unfortunate that Senator Vasconcellos has excluded proponents of other medical marijuana distribution models from the "summit." This seems particularly inappropriate for a member of a party that calls itself "Democratic." It may be that the Democrats are just unaccustomed to backing something that actually has the support of the majority of the people, as does Prop 215. I certainly hope that they will at least consider alternative views. Vasconcellos and AMR should not be so dismissive of their critics, particularly those like Jeff Jones, who has an outstanding record with the Oakland club.
See 

Anything that will get medical marijuana to as many patients as possible -- as quickly as possible -- is morally imperative, but -- to put it very bluntly -- I do not have much more confidence in organized medicine than I have in law enforcement. Of course, my distrust is merely based on 60 years of anecdotal evidence.)
See
